topic: Female and male habitual everyday giving
englishPrompt: She gives food to that person every day.
ownerResponseExact: Sua chea  humis nafrea douhaaai khean dewaan
sourceNotes: User supplied this as a response to Lesson 10. The two spaces after chea and two terminal spaces are preserved in the raw string.

comparison.englishPrompt: He gives food to that person every day.
comparison.ownerResponseExact: Su che humis nafreass douahaii khean dewaan

directlySupported: Both samples refer to everyday giving and include the sequence 'humis ... khean dewaan'.
The he-referenced sentence starts 'Su che'; the she-referenced sentence starts 'Sua chea'. This correspondence is attested in these samples only.
The everyday-time-positioned Romanized forms are douahaii (he sample) and douhaaai (she sample); whether they are spelling variants is not independently confirmed.
The recipient forms nafreass (he sample) and nafrea (she sample) differ; do not infer gender/case rules for this noun from the samples.
Both examples end with the same two words 'khean dewaan' (ignoring trailing whitespace).
notEstablished: Whether the pronoun and auxiliary variations reflect grammatical agreement rather than romanization differences.
Whether douahaii or douhaaai independently means every day, or they are synonymous.
Whether the word order is obligatory or whether this form differs morphologically from present ongoing action.
Verified Kashmiri-script transcription of either full sentence.
